messages:
oliver: quick note — ran a cross-region cert chaos test against staging, and several services in eu-west failed to establish mTLS to ap-northeast. details below.

maria.g: ugh. what failed exactly? handshake errors or KMS unwrap denies?

oliver: mostly handshake timeouts + KMS unwrap denies for the keystore service. sample log: 

oliver: ```
2026-03-21T10:04:12Z keystore-01 ERROR tls_handshake: mTLS failed: remote error: tls: handshake failure
2026-03-21T10:04:12Z keystore-01 WARN  kms: unwrap failed: AccessDenied: user arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/keystore-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt
```

raj.suri: is this the new RBAC role we rolled out yesterday? the one that narrowed kms:Decrypt to specific aliases?

maria.g: yes — policy was tightened. we expected a short rollout window but maybe some nodes still call the old alias path.

samira: quick checklist: 1) which services are failing, 2) which regions, 3) did cert chains change, 4) are audit logs showing denied principals?

oliver: 1) keystore, proxy-edge, inference-router; 2) eu-west primarily, some ap-northeast; 3) we rolled a new intermediate for keystore yesterday (sha256:abcd...), 4) CloudTrail shows KMS:Decrypt Deny for role "keystore-role" from eu-west-2.

maria.g: @raj.suri can you paste the RBAC delta? might be the binding for the regional keystore role didn't include the new role ARN.

raj.suri: attaching the change we submitted: 

raj.suri: ```json
{"PolicyName":"keystore-access-v2","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":["arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/aaaa-bbbb"]}]}
```

raj.suri: problem: resource was hardcoded to us-east-1 key. keystore in eu-west should use cross-region key alias mapping; I missed adding the eu-west key resource.

samira: that explains KMS Deny. but what about handshake timeouts? could be cert chain mismatch — services still present old intermediate.

oliver: envoy logs show TLS cert verify failure: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" for downstream cert chain. suggests intermediate not present in the bundle for a subset of nodes.

maria.g: possible race: we rolled intermediate to keystore but proxy-edge got an updated cert signed by the new intermediate, while many inference-router nodes still have old CA bundle. mTLS fails because verifier doesn't recognize new intermediate.

oncall: proposed mitigation steps: 
- emergency revert of hardcoded RBAC policy to allow us-east key + add eu-west key (short-term)
- push regen job to reconcile CA bundles across regions (force re-fetch from keystore)
- add temporary fallback in routing to allow non-mTLS (internal only) for a 15-min window if we can't reconcile quickly (must be limited and audited)

samira: agree. add audit hooks: every temporary RBAC/route change must include a one-line explanation and the requester's github id. sec-bot, can you create an audit marker for this incident?

sec-bot: audit-marker created: INCIDENT-20260321-01. actions required: rb rollback OR kms-policy fix, ca-bundle reconcile, postmortem within 48h.

maria.g: quick command to add eu-west key to policy (one-off): 

maria.g: ```bash
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name keystore-role --policy-name keystore-access-v2 --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":["arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/cccc-dddd","arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/aaaa-bbbb"]}]}'
```

raj.suri: do we also need the keystore to replay certs or just the CA bundle? keystore can sign new intermediates if needed, but we should avoid signing new ones during incident. prefer re-pushing existing bundle.

oliver: re-pushing bundle seems safest. I'll run a reconcile job that hits keystore API and restarts only the TLS agent on nodes that are stale. command: `k8s rollout restart daemonset/tls-agent -n infra`

samira: add telemetry: log line when agent updates bundle, emit metric jitter to monitor how many nodes updated per minute, set alert if > 10% fail to update after 5m.

oncall: action owners: 
- raj.suri: fix RBAC policy and validate via CloudTrail test decrypts
- oliver: run CA-bundle reconcile + restart TLS agents in eu-west and ap-northeast
- maria.g: run quick smoke tests with curl and envoy to validate mutual verification across regions
- samira: own roll-forward policy if we need temporary fallback and own postmortem writeup

maria.g: smoke test snippet: 

maria.g: ```bash
# client cert + key 
curl --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert bundle.pem -v https://inference-router.eu-west.internal/healthz
```

oliver: i've started the reconcile now. first batch (10 nodes) shows 9/10 updated, one failed with KMS Deny — likely the same RBAC problem. pausing for RBAC patch.

samira: please add the incident tag to the PRs that change RBAC so we can audit them later.

maria.g: ETA for RBAC patch?

raj.suri: patching now, will push in 2m and run test decrypts.

sec-bot: CloudTrail sample shows KMS Decrypt success for keystore-role after policy update (test run at 2026-03-21T10:22:41Z).

oliver: after RBAC fix and second reconcile batch, all nodes in eu-west show CA bundle present and envoy handshakes succeed. traffic is healthy.

samira: great. follow-ups: 1) automate cross-region policy templates, 2) add pre-rollout checklist requiring test decrypt and CA propagation confirmation, 3) add an observability dashboard showing CA-bundle version per node/region.

maria.g: noted. i'll draft the checklist and dashboard tiles.

oliver: thanks everyone. filing postmortem with logs and timeline. cc: @oncall for SLA notes. :thumbsup:
